name: nullable-fields
body: Every field and record-item descriptor in a template.yaml field schema carries `nullable: true|false`, defaulting to false. A non-nullable field rejects a YAML `null` value with the error `got null — this field isn't nullable`. Nullability applies to every field type and to every list-item descriptor: a nullable field accepts an explicit `null` for any field type (text, number, date, boolean, enum, image, link, list, section-template), and a nullable record item descriptor accepts a null list entry — `items: [null]` — which skips the record's `fields:` validation. A null entry runs no bound, format or membership check: `min`/`max`, `min_date`/`max_date`, `max_length`, `min_items`/`max_items`, `formats`/`default_format` and enum-variant membership all skip a null entry. Null is distinct from absent: a `required: true` nullable field requires the key to be present and it may be null, while omitting the key is governed by the required/default rule, and an explicit `null` never triggers the declared `default`. In layouts an absent value and an explicit `null` both reach the context as a nil value; the reserved `.raw` entry preserves the difference (raw-source-context).
